articles.title: Sammer sieht Bayern besser als in der Vorsaison
articles.excerpt: Ex-Sportvorstand Matthias Sammer hat dem FC Bayern ein exzellentes Transferzeugnis ausgestellt und sieht die Mannschaft im Vergleich zum Vorjahr in dieser Saison noch einmal stärker. Selbst in der Champions League sieht
articles.content:
Ex-Sportvorstand Matthias Sammer hat dem FC Bayern ein exzellentes Transferzeugnis ausgestellt und sieht die Mannschaft im Vergleich zum Vorjahr in dieser Saison noch einmal stärker. Selbst in der Champions League sieht er für die Münchner zunächst keine große Hürde.

Geht es nach Matthias Sammer, müssen sich die Gegner des FC Bayern in dieser Saison ganz warm anziehen - sogar noch wärmer als in der Vorsaison, in der die Münchner nicht weit weg vom Triple waren. 

Die Mannschaft des Rekordmeisters habe sich "nicht verschlechtert. Mit Brown und Saibari sind sie noch einen Tick besser", analysierte Sammer bei "Prime Video" und attestierte dem deutschen Branchenprimus damit ein hervorragendes Transferzeugnis. Brown und Saibari sind die beiden namhaftesten Münchner Neuzugänge des Sommers - und werden es bis Transferschluss wohl auch bleiben. 

Auch auf der internationalen Bühne sieht Sammer für den FCB zunächst keine großen Hindernisse. "Ich gehe davon aus, dass Bayern sieben Siege holt", meinte er mit Blick auf die Champions-League-Ligaphase, in der die Bayern unter anderem auf den FC Arsenal, Atlético Madrid und Manchester United treffen. Acht Ligaspiele stehen in der Königsklasse insgesamt für jeden Klub auf dem Programm. 

Eine tragende Rolle in der Champions League traut Sammer aber nicht nur dem FC Bayern zu, sondern auch den anderen deutschen Vertretern. "Es werden alle weitergehen. Bayern direkt und die anderen drei über die Playoffs", ist der ehemalige Profi überzeugt, dass der BVB, der VfB Stuttgart und RB Leipzig ihre Hausaufgaben in der Ligaphase ebenfalls erledigen werden. 

Sammers "Prime"-Kollegen Mats Hummels und Christoph Kramer sind ganz ähnlicher Auffassung. "Ich rechne auch mit allen Teams", sagte Hummels über die K.o.-Chancen der Bundesligisten. Kramer prognostizierte sogar, dass der VfB "ein kräftiges Wörtchen über die Playoff-Runde mitsprechen" kann. Im Finale sieht er am Ende den FC Bayern und den FC Barcelona.

articles.title: Five Things I Like: Week 13
articles.excerpt: Candace Pedraza breaks down five key storylines following week thirteen WNBA action.
articles.content:
• 5 Things I Like
  • Analysis

Five Things I Like: Week 13

Candace Pedraza

We are six days away from the start of the WNBA’s FIBA Women’s World Cup break, which means two things: there will be a pause on WNBA games until September 17 from that point on, and we’ll be catching the league’s stars competing on an international stage with international bragging rights at stake. 

So, we won’t really be all that deprived of a bit of WNBA action, albeit under the guise of watching powerhouses like the United States, France, Belgium, Japan, and others compete for the cup. 

With just over a week left until that break, though, the WNBA was chock-full of moments worth reliving.

Kuier Continues to Shine for Dallas

While Jessica Shepard has been getting a ton of praise for her ascension as a star big while with the Wings this season, Kuier has been an unsung hero on defense for Dallas as they struggle to find consistent rim protection. Her defense, coupled with her capabilities as a stretch 4, has made her a very fun bench piece for head coach Jose Fernandez to plug and play. 

Against the Indiana Fever in a game crucial to Dallas’ seeding, Kuier managed to rack up seven blocks, 11 points, eight boards, and four assists. She also hit two three-pointers to boot. 

After the game, Fever head coach Stephanie White tipped her hat to Kuier and the entire Wings front court, saying, “They have great length.… They did a great job of shelling us, forcing us into a crowd, and not allowing us to see some easy, open teammates. We got to watch the film, and we got to be better.”

Dallas is projected to face off against the Minnesota Lynx in round one of the playoffs if the season ended today. However, postseason seeding is far from settled beyond perhaps the Lynx at 1 and the Golden State Valkyries at 2. If they did face Minnesota, having depth like Kuier to back up Shepard is critical against the Lynx, who boast Natasha Howard next to Napheesa Collier in their frontcourt.

Bueckers’ Perfect Game from 3-point Range

Paige Bueckers #5 of the Dallas Wings

Remaining on the Dallas hype train for a moment, they finished up their weekend with a win over the last-place Seattle Storm. It was a blowout for essentially the entire contest, namely because Paige Bueckers didn’t miss from three-point range. She finished up the game with six threes and 32 total points. 18 of those points came in the 1st quarter.

Bueckers remains the tone setter for the Wings’ offense, while players like Arike Ogunbowale, Shepard, and Kuier contribute around her. With Azzi Fudd out for the year, it’s imperative that they find their offense from everywhere, and not just from three-point range. 

Still, it’s always cool to see a heater like this from Bueckers, who is looking to reach the postseason with the Wings for the first time since getting drafted last year. She has to remain as efficient as possible for the remaining stretch of games that Dallas has in front of them, and luckily for them, they have the second-easiest remaining strength of schedule in the WNBA.

Mitchell Continues to Crawl Up Leaderboard

As you might know, Las Vegas Aces superstar center A’ja Wilson is attempting to win her third straight scoring title this season. She’s at 935 points through August 24, but she has unbelievably stiff competition from Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell. She’s sitting at 967 total points scored through August 24, which means we could see two WNBA players finish up with over 1,000 points scored in a single season. 

Focusing on Mitchell, though, she continued her streak of scoring over 20 points per game this week. She’s upped her points per game average to 24.8, which is a career high. Mitchell, of course, didn’t draw too much attention to the fact that she broke Wilson’s previous record for the number of consecutive 20+ point games after the Fever’s loss to the Wings:

“But I think ultimately it just comes down, obviously, to work. But I don’t really take statistics really that serious. So a lot of this stuff is really circumstantial to me. So I [want] to get the dub, and we didn’t get that. So I think keep my focus on the right thing; keeping the main thing the main thing is important.” 

Mitchell is sneakily climbing into this year’s MVP conversation with this level of production, all of which is the best of her career.

Fiebich Returns with a Bang for New York

Leonie Fiebich #13 of the New York Liberty

While the New York Liberty have had a rough go of things this year, partially due to big injuries to Leonie Fiebich and Satou Sabally, they at least got some good news with the return of Fiebich to the floor ahead of the FIBA break. She immediately contributed on both ends of the floor for New York, posting 20 points, five boards, five assists, and a steal en route to a critical win against the Fever. 

Notably, she also held Clark to 2-7 shooting when she was her primary defender, per ESPN’s Alexa Phillipou. This, amid a hot scoring month for the point guard, is extremely encouraging for New York to see ahead of a potential postseason meet-up with Indiana. 

Fiebich is the kind of x-factor that a contending team like the Liberty needs to go on a deep postseason run. Wings do not grow on trees, and New York is sorely missing the length and defense that they get by plugging Fiebich back into the fold.

Reese Scores First 30-Point Performance

It was just one game, but it might be time to officially put to bed the notion that you can’t run your offense through Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese. 

The third-year star recorded the first 30-point performance of her WNBA career against the Phoenix Mercury in a win. She shot 14-21 from the field, in addition to notching 14 rebounds, four steals, and two assists. 

This is huge for a few reasons, but mainly because Atlanta is better as a unit when Reese can put together huge games on offense like this one. Obviously, they have great weapons like Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray around her. Still, one stat really proves why running some more offense through the third-year forward might be something to focus on: the Dream are 9-2 when she shoots 50 percent from the field or better this season, and just 15-11 when she does not, per CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney. 

Watching this specific game back, you see the potential for this kind of offense – the give-and-go between Reese and basically any of Atlanta’s guards, but especially players like Gray or Howard who have a lot of shooting gravity, is a great means of getting her open as a cutter. She can also use her strength in the post, which is what she did a lot of in this game. Her strengths as a ball handler also make her a threat as a bit of a quarterback keeper, to put it clunkily, as she can fake an outlet pass while running right to the paint for a shot. 

This makes Atlanta scary to face in the postseason and makes the prospect of having to defend Reese even scarier.

articles.title: Can Valkyries overtake Lynx’s top playoff seed? Our WNBA playoff picture forecast
articles.excerpt: There's an intriguing race for the top seed, while on the flip side, get ready for other teams to tank.
articles.content:
Latest

From WNBA

Playoff Picture Forecast
Projection Bracket
Coach Paige Bueckers?
Power Rankings

Can Valkyries overtake Lynx’s top playoff seed? Our WNBA playoff picture forecast

The Valkyries' end-of-season schedule looks ideal for them to keep pushing for a top seed. Elsa / Getty Images

By Sabreena Merchant
Aug. 31, 2026 7:00 am EDT Updated

Take a deep breath. After a fast and furious August featuring last-second game-winners, record-breaking performances and a little too much spiciness on and off the court, the WNBA will press pause for the next 16 days for the FIBA World Cup.

With four games remaining for each team during the regular season, let’s take a look at where we stand.

Advertisement

Playoff field is set

There hasn’t been much intrigue for weeks as to which teams will advance to the postseason, and the Dallas Wings ended any drama by clinching the final playoff spot last week. Although the Phoenix Mercury, Chicago Sky, Los Angeles Sparks and — to some extent — the expansion Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo harbored postseason hopes entering the 2026 season, the eight playoff teams this year will be the Atlanta Dream, Wings, Golden State Valkyries, Indiana Fever, Las Vegas Aces, Minnesota Lynx, New York Liberty and Washington Mystics.

Those team names were listed in alphabetical order with the seeding order still dramatically in flux. As indicated in The Athletic’s playoff projection bracket, the top three seeds are relatively certain: The Lynx are the odds-on favorite (94 percent likelihood) to secure the No. 1 seed, the Valkyries are in position to be the No. 2 seed, and the Aces are right behind them. Beyond that, no team has more than a 40 percent chance of landing at any particular slot. In fact, one of the most curious findings in the projection bracket is that the Dream are the most likely team to finish fourth and fifth, but they obviously can’t play each other in the first round of the postseason.

With so much at stake in the final four games of the season, every game between playoff teams takes on greater importance. Golden State, Las Vegas and Dallas are free and clear of any more postseason previews, but here are the six remaining:

Friday, Sept. 18: New York at Minnesota

Sunday, Sept. 20: Washington at Indiana

Monday, Sept. 21: Atlanta at New York

Tuesday, Sept. 22: Minnesota at Indiana

Wednesday, Sept. 23: Atlanta at New York

Thursday, Sept. 24: Indiana at Minnesota

The Lynx need to win at least one of those games (assuming they also beat the Connecticut Sun) to secure the No. 1 seed and homecourt advantage through the playoffs. Three wins could get New York into the top four and a first-round Game 1 at Barclays Center, and Atlanta probably needs to split with the Liberty to stay in the 4-5 matchup.

Advertisement

Several tiebreakers remain in flux. Indiana’s tiebreakers against New York, Washington and the Dream all have yet to be decided, so there will be no rest before the playoffs tip off.

Who is the championship favorite?

The Lynx have been the top seed for most of the season but head into the break losers of two in a row with Olivia Miles nicked up yet again. She also just had only the second zero assist game of her career, the first coming in a 32-point blowout over Toronto that was a little less consequential.

Minnesota is not nearly as bulletproof as one would expect a top seed to be. Since the All-Star break, the Lynx have the league’s second-best record, but only the fourth-best net rating. Their offense was bottled up against Golden State and their defense suffered against Atlanta. Leaks have been springing for some time in Minnesota.

Perhaps it’s not a surprise, then, that the Lynx have been usurped as the title favorite, per our projection bracket. That honor now goes to the Valkyries, coming off a week when they won on the road in Minnesota and New York. Golden State’s defense has been phenomenal all year, and their offense has perked up lately, in part thanks to the drives of Tiffany Hayes. No one can keep her out of the paint.

Watch This: Hayes, Chen lead Valkyries past Fire

The Valkyries would be a unique title winner. It’s rare for a WNBA champion to be without a single no-brainer MVP candidate. In the last 17 years, only the 2021 Sky didn’t have a first-team All-WNBA player.

Maybe the Aces should still be considered a title favorite with their prodigious top-end talent. Even without NaLyssa Smith, Las Vegas has a roster full of proven playoff performers, a head coach with a 10-1 record in playoff series and A’ja Wilson, who is the best player alive. Then again, if the Aces matched up with the Liberty in the first round, an early exit against a team that can take advantage of its lack of size wouldn’t exactly be surprising.

Advertisement

The Fever have the best offense in WNBA history, and this league has historically rewarded offense over defense. Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark can go on heaters that many other teams can’t keep up with, but Indiana’s offense can sometimes be bogged down by full-court pressure.

I tend to believe there is no championship favorite at this point. Expansion of the league by 25 percent in the last two seasons has created a little too much parity, giving several teams an opportunity to emerge victorious this postseason.

Prepare for an epic tank-off

The pandemic years are long behind us, but the issue of college eligibility hasn’t yet been settled. The NCAA’s new five-in-five rule means that the 2027 draft class won’t be decided until much closer to April, since all of the best prospects can choose to return to college for one more season.

The uncertainty of who could be available hasn’t stopped several franchises from, let’s just say, incentivizing their odds of landing a top pick by accumulating as many losses as possible. As a result, the lottery standings are almost as compelling as the playoff race.

Four games remain between a pair of non-playoff teams, and two of them stand out. The first is on Sept. 20 between Portland and Los Angeles. Neither team has let go of the rope to end the season; both collected surprising wins against playoff-bound opponents last week and have looked a cut better than the rest of their lottery-destined peers. To wit: Carla Leite proved wholly deserving of her first invite to a major senior tournament for France by dropping 26 points and six assists in a rout over Atlanta. Meanwhile, Nneka Ogwumike looks like she could command a multi-year max contract in free agency despite just announcing her retirement.

The Fire and Sparks are in fifth and sixth position in the lottery standings, but they could flip if Portland wins at Los Angeles. Neither spot has a great chance of securing the No. 1 pick, but the odds from fifth-place are about twice as good. The main reason to pick the Sparks in this particular matchup is that Ogwumike has been vocal about her desire to play the right way to close out the season, and coach Lynne Roberts has said that finishing strong — despite the potential harm to the Sparks’ lottery odds — is the best way to honor the franchise legend. Considering L.A.’s only other home game after the break is against Golden State, this might be the best opportunity to send Ogwumike out in style.

Ogwumike isn't slowing down
Sabreena Merchant

The other truly tanktastic matchup comes on the last day of the regular season between Connecticut and Toronto. The Sun have been on a methodical two-year teardown, and the fruit of their labor would be top odds for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft. On the other hand, the Tempo were seemingly angling for a playoff bid in 2026 but pivoted due to a rash of injuries. As an expansion team, this is the only opportunity for team to execute a one-year tank, and Toronto has worked its way to the bottom, winning one of its last 17 games. Good luck recognizing all of the players in the lineups that the Tempo are putting out: In their latest miserable loss to Phoenix, three of their bench players weren’t even in camp to start the season.

It’s possible that the two teams might enter the final day with Toronto needing one more loss to tie Connecticut for the worst two-year win percentage, which would result in splitting the top odds. And the poor Sun will be saying goodbye to Connecticut on a day when a win would be the worst thing that could happen to them.

Aug 31, 2026

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must now work together at Women's World Cup as WNBA takes a high-stakes break
articles.excerpt: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must set aside their WNBA rivalry and build team chemistry as Team USA defends its title at the Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin.
articles.content:
OutKick Sports

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese must now work together at Women's World Cup as WNBA takes a high-stakes break

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese's chemistry, and what happens during the national anthem are key questions for the US

By Jackson Thompson OutKick
Published August 31, 2026 6:51am EDT
  • Comments
  • Facebook
  • Twitter
  • Threads
  • Flipboard
  • Print
  • Email
  • Add Fox News on Google
close
Video

Jackson Thompson Exposes the WNBA’s Biggest Problem

OutKick Reporter Jackson Thompson joins Riley Gaines to break down what he’s seeing inside the WNBA’s biggest cultural moment. Riley and Jackson discuss Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham, the Indiana Fever, WNBA fan energy, league growth, media gatekeeping, and whether the league is prepared for its expanding audience. They also discuss the ongoing debate over men in women’s sports, questions around WNBA eligibility policies, Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White, San Jose State volleyball, and how sports media has covered female athletes speaking out. Plus, Jackson shares what he’s watching next as the WNBA postseason approaches and Team USA women’s basketball prepares for international competition.

The U.S. is headed to a battle in Berlin.

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese will have to work together to uphold American dominance in the Women's Basketball World Cup in September. At home, the WNBA will take a two-week break from hosting the chaos of the 2026 season.

So Americans will have to root together for their biggest stars on the world stage. The U.S. has won four consecutive World Cups in a row and this year's team will also have to protect an active 30-game win streak.

What happens in Berlin could very well shape the climate of the league that the players return to when the WNBA season resumes.

 

Can Clark and Reese work together?

Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark of the USA Women's National Team look on during a game against Puerto Rico during the 2026 FIBA World Cup Qualifying Tournament on March 12, 2026, at Coliseo Jose Miguel Agrelot in San Juan, Puerto Rico. (NBAE via Getty Images)

Clark and Reese have spent more than three years framed as adversaries.

The last time they were on a basketball court, Clark was seen laughing as she walked by Reese, who had just missed the game-winning layup.

Their rivalry fueled the 2023 national championship game between Iowa and LSU. It followed them into a rematch in the 2024 NCAA Tournament, then into the WNBA as the top two contenders for Rookie of the Year. Every matchup, foul and postgame comment became another invitation for fans to choose a side.

But at times, they've also shown glimpses of what that can look like when playing together.

Reese first said, "one day, hopefully, we can be teammates," while discussing Clark in an October 2024 Wall Street Journal article.

They first became teammates at the 2024 WNBA All-Star Game, when Clark recorded 10 assists and Reese finished with 12 points and 11 rebounds in Team WNBA’s victory over the U.S. Olympic team.

CAITLIN CLARK HELPS WNBA SHATTER ANOTHER TV RATINGS RECORD AS FEVER-DREAM DRAWS MASSIVE AUDIENCE

In March, Clark and Reese helped the U.S. go 5-0 at the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico.

There was an awkward moment when Clark appeared to ignore a high five invitation from Reese during one of the games.

Clark earned tournament MVP honors after averaging 11.6 points and a tournament-leading 6.4 assists. Reese averaged a team-high eight rebounds while shooting 52.2% from the field.

"Team chemistry is everything," Reese said during the qualifying tournament. "Some of us have played with each other on our respective teams, but we have to come together and find your role. Everybody’s not going to be able to do everything that they do on their respective team."

Clark and Reese will play alongside established champions A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier and Chelsea Gray in Berlin.

 

What will happen during the national anthems?

Team Coop stands for the national anthem before the 2026 WNBA All-Star Game at the United Center in Chicago. (NBAE via Getty Images)

The available rules and national-team precedent point to the entire U.S. team standing on the court for "The Star-Spangled Banner" in Berlin. Whether every player places her hand over her heart or sings along is a separate question that neither USA Basketball nor FIBA rules answer.

The issue has drawn new attention during the 2026 WNBA season because teams have followed different routines.

Several WNBA teams historically and routinely remain in the locker room or clear the floor during the playing of the national anthem as part of pregame routines.

CHINA’S INFLUENCE MACHINE: FEDERAL RECORDS EXPOSE BEIJING’S PUSH TO SWAY AMERICA

The Atlanta Dream remained in their locker room while the anthem played before their Aug. 16 game against the Indiana Fever. That left Reese and Rhyne Howard, both members of the World Cup roster, off the court while Clark, Aliyah Boston and the rest of the Fever stood along the sideline.

Clark stood facing the flag with her hands behind her back. Sophie Cunningham placed her right hand over her heart.

The difference generated criticism of Clark online, although nothing in the WNBA rulebook requires players to sing or place a hand over their heart.

Sophie Cunningham and Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever stand for the national anthem before a game against the Chicago Sky at United Center in Chicago, Ill., on Aug. 8, 2026. (Getty Images)

The rules change when those players leave their WNBA teams and join the national program.

USA Basketball’s code of conduct requires participants to follow FIBA and USA Basketball rules, attend team functions as directed and "demonstrate proper respect during the playing of the national anthem." The code does not define "proper respect," but it gives USA Basketball authority to investigate alleged violations and impose discipline.

FIBA also controls the ceremonies in Berlin. Its 2026 regulations state that only anthems and flags of countries or national federations recognized by FIBA may be used. The regulations leave the details of World Cup ceremonies to the tournament’s hosting documents. They do not publicly prescribe whether a player must sing, place a hand over her heart or assume another specific posture.

FIBA’s code of conduct additionally prohibits players and other "basketball parties" from using gestures, words or objects to transmit political or ideological messages that are deemed unfit for a sporting event. The rule does not specifically identify kneeling, remaining silent or declining to place a hand over the heart as violations. It does, however, give FIBA greater control over demonstrations than the WNBA has exercised during its domestic season.

Past U.S. teams have treated international competition differently from the WNBA. American players who routinely remained off the court during WNBA anthems stood together for them at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics. Sue Bird, then the team’s captain and now the managing director who selected the 2026 roster, said wearing a USA uniform changed the context.

"You are wearing USA jerseys and it does change the conversation a little bit and what you’re representing," Bird said at the time. "With that, I don’t feel like a hypocrite in any way. Everyone knows where we stand. I don’t think it contradicts anything since we’re actually doing the work." The U.S. players stood with their arms linked during that Olympic run.

There also were no reported anthem protests during the United States’ five-game World Cup qualifying run in Puerto Rico in March. That team included Clark, Reese, Howard, Paige Bueckers and Kahleah Copper.

As of Aug. 30, no member of the World Cup roster has publicly announced plans to kneel, leave the floor or conduct another demonstration during the anthem in Berlin.

 

Rival world powers collide

Flags of the U.S. and China sit in a room where U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken meets with China's Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, April 26, 2024, in Beijing, China. (Mark Schiefelbein/Pool via REUTERS/File photo)

The Americans will open the World Cup against China on Sept. 4. It will be a rematch of the 2022 World Cup final. Women's basketball dominance over America's greatest current geopolitical rival will be on the line.

There have been 15 World Cup and Olympic meetings between the countries, and the U.S. has won all 15.

Two of those victories came at the 2022 World Cup. The U.S. beat China 77-63 during group play and then defeated it again, 83-61, in the final. The victory gave the Americans their fourth consecutive world championship.

China still viewed its silver medal as a major national achievement. The championship game took place on Oct. 1, China’s National Day.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Afterward, China’s General Administration of Sport praised the team for competing "with the motherland in mind." The government agency called the silver medal "a perfect birthday gift to the country," according to China Daily.

What happens during national anthems will also be a point of potential contrast during the game against China.

China has had a national anthem law since 2017. The law specifically lists major sporting events as occasions for the anthem and directs those present to stand solemnly and behave respectfully. Deliberately insulting the anthem in public can result in detention or criminal prosecution under Chinese law.

The law will not govern what the American players do in Berlin. But it shows how differently the two countries can treat displays of patriotism at sporting events.

In the U.S., anthem protests have become part of the political debate surrounding professional sports. Players have been praised, criticized and placed under close scrutiny depending on whether they stand, kneel, leave the court or place a hand over their heart.

In China, disrespecting the anthem can become a legal matter.

The World Cup opener will arrive amid another sensitive period in U.S.-China relations. The countries remain divided over trade, tariffs, human rights and China’s relationship with Taiwan, even as officials work toward another meeting between their presidents.

None of that will determine what happens on the court. But it will affect how the game—and especially the moments before it — are interpreted in both countries.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: JD Vance set to address Jewish conservatives, as some Jews in GOP share concerns about his recent Israel remarks
articles.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance is set to address a gathering of Jewish conservatives on Monday, even as some Jews in the GOP have raised concerns about his remarks on Israel.
articles.content:
JD Vance set to address Jewish conservatives, as some Jews in GOP share concerns about his recent Israel remarks

Some Jews in GOP say his attendance at the event is a positive sign.

ByOren Oppenheim
August 31, 2026, 6:06 AM

Vice President JD Vance is set to address a major gathering of Jewish conservatives on Monday, with some Jews in the GOP raising concerns that the vice president is breaking with them on Israel -- and others saying his attendance at the event is a positive sign.

Vance is set to speak at the Republican Jewish Coalition (RJC) annual leadership summit in Las Vegas, Nevada, just hours after a campaign stop in Michigan.

But while the RJC is staunchly supportive of Israel, the vice president has made sharp and skeptical comments toward Israel in recent months, contrasting with the party faithful's traditionally supportive line toward the Jewish state.

While delivering a press briefing in the White House in June, for instance, as the United States was working on a deal to pause the war started by the U.S. and Israel with Iran, Vance told reporters that he had seen Israeli Cabinet members criticize the deal and would tell them that "Donald J. Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time ... If I was in the Cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world."

Related
Texas GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton works to overcome fundraising woes, with President Trump's help

In a later interview with podcaster Joe Rogan, Vance also said that "there are some people" in the Israeli government "we know beyond a shadow of a doubt who are manipulating and trying to change American public opinion to keep the war going on indefinitel. ... what I would say to the Americans who sort of see this and are frustrated by it, my attitude would be: you should be frustrated at American leaders who are persuaded by this, affected by this."

Vance also said other governments run similar influence campaigns. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told ABC News he spoke with Vance about those comments "and I think we straightened that out because we're not. That's not our policy."

Vance, in a later Fox News interview where he was asked about reported discordant conversations with Netanyahu, said that Israel is "a great partner" but that he was willing to have "a frank conversation" with Netanyahu when their viewpoints differ, similar to conversations with other U.S. allies.

Maura Schrier-Fleming, who is a member of a Dallas-based group of Jewish Republican women, told ABC News that she found some of Vance's comments about Israel's actions in the region to be "a mischaracterization of how Israel has had to defend itself."

Asked what she'd be looking to hear from Vance at the conference, Schrier-Fleming said, "He's got to emphasize that what's good for America is good for Americans, and our ally, our only democratic ally in the Middle East, has demonstrated to America that they are worth more than the aid we provide them."

Related
Trump announces Republicans' first midterm convention in September

A veteran Republican operative, who asked not to be named as he is actively working in Republican politics, pointed to Vance's White House briefing as an inflection point to how Vance has been discussed among Jewish Republicans, saying that Vance's support among Jewish conservatives collapsed tremendously after he said that.

The operative felt that further efforts by Vance to reach out to Jewish conservatives or to show support for Israel was akin to an "apology tour," as well as a calculation toward winning back support among the Jewish right ahead of a potential run for president in 2028. Vance has declined to confirm if he plans to run for the presidency in 2028, saying he is focused on the midterms, but has left the door open to a run.

Both Vance and Trump have aired disagreements with Netanyahu, with the president confirming to Axios in mid-June that he had excoriated Netanyahu over a strike in Lebanon.

In the Fox interview, Vance also framed his dissent with Israel as part of a partnership with the ally, saying, "When our interests are aligned with Israel, we talk about how to accomplish those shared objectives. When my viewpoint is averse to the Prime Minister of Israel, we have a frank conversation about that."

Beyond discussions of Israel, Vance has also condemned antisemitism on numerous occasions, allaying other potential concerns of Jewish conservatives.

Some Jewish conservatives have pushed back on the notion that there's any divide between Vance and Jewish Republicans on Israel.

Y. David Scharf, an attorney who is a major donor to Republicans, told ABC News by email that he recently spoke with Vance "about shared themes in Judaism and Catholicism," and that "as for Israel, I can speak from my own interactions with him, where he has been unequivocal in expressing support for the U.S.-Israel alliance."

Related
'It's his decision': Netanyahu says choice on how to proceed with Iran is Trump's

Some Republican Jewish conservatives have also said they feel the fact that Vance is going to the RJC in the first place is a positive sign that he wants to reconnect with Jewish conservatives and to have conversations about Israel.

Eric Levine, a major fundraiser for GOP Senate candidates, told ABC News, "The fact that he's coming to speak to us, I think, is a very good thing."

Levine is a board member of the RJC, but spoke to ABC News in a personal capacity, not on behalf of the organization.

"The fact that he's coming to speak to us, I think, is a very good thing. He's reaching out to the Jewish community... and not just the Jewish community, but anyone who supports the American-Israeli relationship and wants to fight antisemitism," Levine said.

articles.content:
Prognosen der TV-Experten: Kramer prophezeit Königsklassen-Finale Barcelona - Bayern

Mats Hummels, Christoph Kramer und Matthias Sammer werden wieder bei Champions-League-Übertragungen ihre Meinung äußern. Was das Trio von den vier deutschen Clubs erwartet.

Stand: heute, 13:46 Uhr

Die TV-Experten und früheren Nationalspieler Mats Hummels, Matthias Sammer und Christoph Kramer rechnen damit, dass alle vier deutschen Clubs in die K.-o.-Runde der Champions League einziehen. „Ich sage: Finale Barcelona - Bayern“, prophezeite Ex-Weltmeister Kramer in einer digitalen Pressekonferenz des übertragenden Senders Prime Video vor der Königsklassen-Gruppenphase. 

„Bayern ist ein Favorit, aber nicht der Topfavorit. Ich sehe die fünf, sechs üblichen Verdächtigen“, sagte der ehemalige Münchner und Dortmunder Fußballprofi Hummels. Kramer geht davon aus, dass der BVB „am zweitweitesten kommt. Ich glaube, dass Stuttgart ein kräftiges Wort über die Play-off-Runde hinaus mitsprechen kann.“ 

„Streitbare Konstellation mit José Mourinho“

Bei der Frage nach den Titelkandidaten nannte der ehemalige Europameister und heutige Borussia-Berater Sammer die Bayern („Sie haben sich nicht verschlechtert“), Titelverteidiger Paris Saint-Germain, den FC Arsenal („Ich finde, Arsenal muss sich nach der Meisterschaft erst mal wieder beweisen“), Real Madrid („Eine streitbare Konstellation mit José Mourinho“) sowie den FC Barcelona („Werden eine gute Rolle spielen“).

„Sie sind die Besten der Welt“

Der 58-Jährige geht davon aus, dass der Meister aus München sieben von acht Spielen in der Ligaphase gewinnt: „Sie sind die Besten der Welt, in Europa sowieso. Bei Dortmund habe ich mich auf fünf Siege festgelegt. RB hat in meinen Augen die schwerste Gruppe.“ 

Die Münchner starten ihren nächsten Angriff auf den Triumph in der Champions League mit einem Heimspiel gegen den norwegischen Club Bodö/Glimt am 10. September und treffen später unter anderem auf Arsenal und Atlético Madrid. Dortmund empfängt zum Start am 8. September den FC Villarreal. RB Leipzig reist zum Debütanten Como 1907 am 10. September. Der VfB Stuttgart spielt am 9. September daheim gegen Neuling Viking Stavanger.

US Agencies Forced Down a Drone Over White Sands After Suspected Surveillance Flight
Monday, 31 August 2026, 13:20

The entrance to White Sands Missile Range near White Sands, New Mexico, photographed on February 21, 2024. Valerie Macon/AFP/Getty Images

A drone’s five-day intrusion over a restricted US missile range triggered an unusually broad response and raised questions about hidden surveillance.

In spring 2025, U.S. agencies intercepted a quadcopter that had violated the restricted airspace over White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico for approximately five days. The drone’s flight path suggested it may have been conducting reconnaissance of the military facility.

Based on data from CNN

The operation involved the U.S. Army, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon unit that analyzes unidentified anomalous phenomena. Electronic warfare measures forced the drone to land in a parking lot.

A Camper Van and Chinese Nationals Near a Military Base

At the same time, law enforcement officers were monitoring several Chinese nationals near White Sands. They arrived in the United States, rented a Mercedes camper van, and drove across the country to the missile range.

Separately, officials identified a Chinese woman who drove a rental car to White Sands National Park and remained there after it closed. The group in the camper van was detained by military personnel and later handed over to federal authorities. The woman was fined and released.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation suspected that the detained individuals could be linked to Chinese intelligence. Their subsequent fate has not been disclosed.

Claims that China is engaged in espionage are entirely without factual basis or evidence and are nothing more than unfounded speculation and sensational exaggeration.

– Spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy

Helicopters and a Drone Chase Over White Sands

The incident in spring 2025 was not the first time a suspicious drone had appeared over the military facility. In the fall of 2024, border agents pursued a similar drone over White Sands for about 56 kilometers, deploying helicopters and their own unmanned aircraft.

After the aircraft crossed the border into Mexico, the pursuit was called off. U.S. officials emphasize that not all illegal drone flights show signs of espionage. Drones are also launched by hobbyists, tourists, and criminal groups, which may use them to transport drugs.

Laser Systems Against Drones and Risks for the United States

The availability of inexpensive drones has made protecting U.S. military bases and critical infrastructure a separate challenge. For a long time, no agency had clearly defined responsibility for responding to such threats.

Following a series of incidents, U.S. Northern Command began coordinating responses to small drones appearing over military bases. The Pentagon is expanding its arsenal of countermeasures, including laser systems, high-powered microwave systems, and electronic warfare tools.

At the same time, the use of such technologies has already caused problems. In February, the airspace over El Paso was closed because of a poorly coordinated test of a laser system. Later, the military mistakenly shot down a U.S. Customs and Border Protection drone with a laser.

New Powers to Combat Drones

In 2026, the U.S. Congress expanded the powers of the Central Intelligence Agency, state authorities, and local police to force down drones that may threaten critical sites.

Counterintelligence specialists acknowledge that establishing a direct link between a specific drone flight and Chinese intelligence services is extremely difficult. In 2024, Chinese national Yinpiaо Zhou was detained for flying a drone over Vandenberg Space Force Base during the launch of a military satellite.

Zhou was sentenced to four months in federal prison for violating restricted airspace rules. U.S. officials believe that drone defense systems are gradually improving, but military facilities and critical infrastructure in the United States remain vulnerable.

articles.title: Helicopter chases, lasers and a rented RV: Inside the hunt for suspected Chinese drone spies over US military bases | CNN Politics
articles.excerpt: It was spring of 2025 and the hunt was on.
articles.content:
See all topics
Email
Link Copied!

It was spring 2025 and the hunt was on.

American authorities near a sensitive Army missile testing facility in New Mexico had spotted a quadcopter-style drone flying in such a way that suggested it was conducting reconnaissance in restricted airspace around the range.

It wasn’t the first time. Just months earlier, in fall 2024, a similar drone was seen flying a similar pattern over the same base, leading agents with US Customs and Border Protection on a roughly 35-mile chase, multiple current and former US officials said.

Using helicopters and drones and taking “absolutely beautiful video,” a former US official said, the border agents tailed the drone until it crossed into Mexican airspace, where they had to turn back. They never learned who was operating the drone, or why.

But this time, officials set a trap.

For roughly five days, amid dust storms and bad weather, the drone flew in and out over White Sands Missile Range. A task force made up of officials from a hodgepodge of agencies — the Army, the FBI, the Department of Homeland Security, even the small office in the Pentagon that tracks UFOs — studied the drone’s patterns of movement, collected intelligence on it, and tried to understand who was operating it and why.

Finally, using electronic warfare tools, they forced the drone to land in a parking lot on the base. Their first step was to make sure the drone wasn’t armed with explosives, according to the former official familiar with the incident.

Meanwhile, officials were watching a group of Chinese nationals in a rented Mercedes RV parked nearby. According to the former US official and another source familiar with the matter, the people had flown into New York, rented the RV, and driven across the country to Las Vegas to pick up a third person before turning south and beelining for White Sands.

There was another person nearby, too: a Chinese woman who had arrived in Texas on a cruise ship, rented a car and driven to White Sands National Park nearby, where she would remain behind the gates after the park’s closing.

Later, both of the sources said, the FBI would tell military and CBP officials that the people were believed to have ties to Chinese intelligence.

Officials watched the two vehicles, trying to understand how they related to each other and to the drone itself.

Eventually, both groups were detained: The group in the RV was picked up by military officials near the base and turned over to federal authorities, according to the source familiar with the incident.

The woman in the park was ticketed and released by the Department of the Interior, according to the former US official.

CNN was unable to learn what happened to any of them afterward. But officials were sure the two groups were connected: According to one of the sources, identifying information related to the woman was found in the RV.

The Army and the FBI did not respond to a request for comment before publication. CBP declined to comment on the specific incident, citing routine policy against commenting on reported incursions. A spokesperson with the Chinese Embassy denied knowledge of the episode.

“The false narrative regarding China engaging in espionage activities is entirely devoid of factual basis or evidence, consisting of nothing more than baseless speculation and sensationalist hype,” the spokesperson said.

The espionage needle in the drone haystack

The episode is one of countless incursions by drones into US airspace over military facilities and other restricted government areas, often flown by hobbyists, cartels ferrying drugs to a third destination, or tourists — but sometimes believed to be flown by foreign agents conducting spy operations.

The proliferation of cheap, easy-to-operate drone technology has made it relatively simple for ordinary people to conduct what at least appears to be drone surveillance — and incredibly difficult for the US government to track and prevent it. That new, chaotic reality has left the government scrambling to catch up.

An Anvil drone interceptor launches from its platform, as if in response to a drone threat, during an exercise at Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, on October 23, 2025.

The nature of any ties to Chinese or other intelligence services is often frustratingly opaque to counterintelligence officials across the government. Investigations involve a matter of gut instinct and guesswork that make it hard to secure more than a petty prosecution for operating a drone in a restricted airspace, current and former officials say.

China is believed to pressure or incentivize ordinary civilians into doing what one official termed “nuisance surveillance” over a variety of military targets, some highly sensitive, some less so. In other instances, those sources say, Chinese nationals inside the US appear to take it upon themselves to spy with no direct order from a Chinese intelligence official.

US officials are worried about the potential for something worse: a lone-wolf-style terrorist attack on critical US infrastructure or civilian targets. Although two US officials with knowledge of the latest intelligence said there’s no indication of an active plot by Iranian proxy groups or other terror groups like ISIS, the obvious opportunity is there.

The recent theft of 15 pesticide drones in New Jersey deeply alarmed American officials, one of the officials said, because of their potential as a delivery system for a chemical weapons attack. Authorities eventually recovered the drones.

Related video

CNN maps how Kyiv is changing the face of modern warfare

3:40

Military officials are also publicly warning that a swarm of drones could overwhelm air defenses in the US homeland. One military official described a Ukrainian drone operation in June 2025, dubbed Operation Spiderweb, as a sobering depiction of what’s possible. Ukraine used 117 drones to destroy at least a dozen Russian warplanes parked at air bases thousands of miles from the front lines.

Those fears have sparked an energetic push across the government to develop and field sophisticated counter-drone equipment to a broad group of authorities — including state and local police and military bases.

The White Sands operation was deemed a success by US authorities​, according to two people involved or briefed on the operation, showcasing a successful interagency process.

But the problem is much bigger than White Sands. And just who in the US government is supposed to be in charge, nobody is quite sure.

“The problem is it’s everyone’s problem — so it’s no one’s problem,” said one US official.

‘It was a circus, it was embarrassing’

There is no single body in the US responsible for detecting, deterring or defeating these incursions in either government or civilian airspace — what the national security community now short-hands as “C-UAS,” or counter-unmanned aircraft systems.

In late 2023 under President Joe Biden, when a mysterious swarm of drones flew over an Air Force base in Virginia for 17 days, some officials who worked on the situation described it as a leaderless free-for-all.

The situation was so chaotic that officials in the Joint Chiefs of Staff — a part of the military that is supposed to advise, not participate in operations — stepped in to create a task force to try to bring order to the situation, according to one of the former US officials.

“It was a circus, it was embarrassing,” this person said. “That’s not in their mandate. But they saw a vacuum.”

Related article
CAMP PENDLETON, CA - JULY 26: View of the main entrance to Camp Pendleton on July 26, 2019 in Oceanside, California. Sixteen Marines were arrested at Camp Pendleton Thursday morning during battalion formation for various illegal activities ranging from human smuggling to drug-related offenses. (Photo by Sandy Huffaker/Getty Images)

Drones continue to buzz over US bases. The military isn’t sure why or how to stop them

6 min read

After that incident, then-Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin designated Northern Command, the military command responsible for homeland defense, as the coordinating authority for small drone incursions at bases.

Since then, Northern Command has established a protocol: Whenever an errant drone is spotted over a military base, it convenes a teleconference between the base, local law enforcement, FBI, DHS, the military services and anybody else who might have a counter-drone system nearby. If the base isn’t capable of mounting its own defenses, they sort out who’s going to transport it and pay for its use.

That system has worked well, the military official said.

“I’ve seen it move from, ‘Who owns [the problem]?’ to, ‘We all own it, and we all have a role to play in it,’” this person said.

Sometimes, the Pentagon office tasked with identifying and analyzing “Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena” — the government’s term for UFOs — is also called because it has specialized equipment designed to track flying objects of an unknown origin. As it did in White Sands, the UAP office can provide a common operating picture for officials tracking drones.

The Pentagon in 2025 also established a task force to coordinate counter-drone technology and techniques across the military. It is exploring directed energy weapons such as lasers and high-powered microwaves that officials hope can cheaply disable drones. DHS in January established a similar office.

There have still been prominent failures.

In two back-to-back misadventures in February, the Federal Aviation Administration closed the airspace over El Paso, Texas, after the Defense Department failed to coordinate with the aviation agency before it allowed CBP to test a counter-drone laser system, sources told CNN at the time. The move effectively shut down the city’s airport for eight hours.

About two weeks later, the US military accidentally shot down an unmanned aircraft operated by CBP with a laser about 50 miles south of El Paso.

Security personnel outside El Paso International Airport on February 11, 2026, after the US Federal Aviation Administration lifted its temporary closure of the airspace.

When it comes to federal facilities, large civilian gatherings and critical infrastructure — installations not under the military’s authority to protect — federal officials have responded by trying to expand the number of entities with access to counter-drone training and equipment and the authority to use it.

The CIA received new authorities from Congress in 2026 for its police to disable drones in the air in the US and force them to the ground when they threaten agency facilities. Congress also expanded state and local governments’ ability to do the same, amid a recognition by lawmakers that no single federal agency could protect against the sheer number of illegal drone flights across the country.

DHS and the FBI have provided extensive support for large, public gatherings — classic “soft targets” — in recent months. Earlier this year, federal officials charged multiple people who they claimed discussed plots to use drones and a gunman to attack a UFC event at the White House. The FBI established no-drone zones around World Cup sites this year, and said that by the week before the final match, it had detected nearly 1,600 illegal drones and confiscated more than 700.

But officials say there are still some gaping security vulnerabilities. One example, according to one of the US officials: No one is sure who is responsible for protecting the data centers that are privately owned but house an enormous amount of sensitive government data for agencies like the CIA.

Right now, it’s the purview of local law enforcement — who may not have the capabilities they need to defend against the threat.

The China problem

When it comes to apparent espionage efforts by China to use drones to spy on military sites in the United States, officials struggle to describe the scope of the problem. This is largely because confidently attributing any one incursion to a Chinese intelligence operation is almost impossible. Officials say that China uses civilian cut-outs to do its dirty work — students and Chinese-origin Americans with family in mainland China whom they can pressure — not trained intelligence officers.

“It’s not like MSS officers are just running wild through the US,” one of the US officials said, referring to China’s espionage service.

In fall 2024, federal officials caught a Chinese national piloting a drone over Vandenberg Space Force Base during a military satellite launch, arresting him at the San Francisco airport as he prepared to board a flight to China. Investigators found aerial photos on his devices of locations in Arkansas, Texas and China. But ultimately, prosecutors were able to only secure a guilty plea from 34-year-old Yinpiao Zhou for flying a small drone into restricted airspace.

A second charge, for failure to register an aircraft, was dismissed as part of the plea agreement. Zhou was sentenced to four months in federal custody.

During the 2023 episode over the Virginia Air Force base, Coast Guard personnel boarded a Chinese-flagged frigate off the East Coast under the guise of a routine safety check, according to multiple sources. But they found nothing definitive to link the ship to the drones.

A drone, used as a ground-to-air and air-to-air enemy drone interceptor, hovers above the trees at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, April 23, 2026.

Current and former US officials say the number of instances of true Chinese espionage flights is likely relatively low.

China’s intelligence-gathering apparatus is “decentralized,” one former counterintelligence official said. Communist party authorities make public their priorities, and “intelligence entrepreneurs” sometimes take it upon themselves to try to collect information that would be valuable, this person said.

The FBI is often tracking Chinese nationals who do strange things: “Driving for 24 straight hours, sleeping in their car, and then go home,” for example, that person said. “That kind of stuff happens a lot, it’s weird, sometimes it’s unexplained.”

Within the government, US officials often seem to speak definitively about attribution, a kind of wink-wink-nudge-nudge suggestion that a given incursion was China.

But because it’s so hard to definitively link any one strange behavior or drone flight to a specific directive from the Chinese intelligence services, some officials think the threat is overblown.

“A lot of these people are guilty of just being Chinese,” the former counterintelligence official said, adding that most of the operators the FBI encounters are hobbyists.

As for a broader campaign of coordinated Chinese surveillance drones in the US?

“I look at this as a conspiracy theory in the making,” the former official said.

Were the people at White Sands more than just low-level cut-outs or “intelligence entrepreneurs”? Officials at DHS and the Defense Department came away with the impression that the FBI thought so. How firm that attribution really was, CNN was unable to determine.

The operation at White Sands, the other former US official said, was “a success story.”

“But we’re far from being done and we’re still very, very vulnerable.”

The Walking Dead: Dead City Brings Back Beth — And Brings Maggie And Negan Closer Than Ever

By Dave Nemetz Aug. 30, 2026 10:10 pm EST
AMC

What is a "Walking Dead" show without any, you know, walking dead? We found out this week when "The Walking Dead: Dead City" showed us an alternate reality where the zombie apocalypse never happened, Beth is alive and well... and Maggie and Negan might actually hit it off.

Sunday's episode starts out where we left off, with Negan having just killed Fabian as well as Dillard's walker pal Cockenspiel. He remembers telling Maggie, "I think we could've been friends in another life," and he hears Dillard whistling outside the front door and pulls his gun. But when the door opens, it's actually Beth — hi, Emily Kinney! — who glides through a sunny bar full of patrons. We're suddenly in a blissfully zombie-free world, and Beth heads to the park to meet her sister Maggie, who's in town for a visit. Beth wants her to stay overnight and see her play guitar at the bar, but Maggie insists she needs to fly back home to Georgia tonight. Their dad has died (R.I.P., Hershel), and Maggie is trying to find a way to not sell the family farm. Beth thinks selling might not be a bad thing, though: "I want you to live your own life, too."

We learn that Maggie is unhappily married to a guy named Danny, and he won't sign the divorce papers; he's harassing her with phone calls when she sits down at a diner. A man across the counter recognizes her Georgia accent and introduces himself: Yep, it's Negan.

Is this the Walking Dead version of a meet-cute?

AMC

This alt-reality Negan is pretty nosy, actually, peppering Maggie with questions about her husband while he wolfs down a huge breakfast. He was married once, too, but she died of cancer. (R.I.P., Lucille.) Maggie tells him she runs her family farm, and he laughs: "There is not a farmer in the history of the world that looks like you." (OK, flirt!) Negan offers to show her around the city, but she tells him she needs to head to the airport soon — but she does agree to stop and get some of those roasted chestnuts first. ("They smell better than they taste," Negan warns — and he's right.) It's Christmastime in the city, and that reminds Maggie of her late mom, who used to have a Statue of Liberty snow globe. Her flight is in six hours, but Negan says that's enough time to join him for lunch.

He takes her to a fancy restaurant, where they order steaks and Negan reviews her business plan to keep the farm running. It's good, he says, but "good, sadly, isn't good enough." She knows it's a sinking ship, and Negan encourages her to get off it before it sinks her, too. He also raises a glass to some men at another table, and soon, a staffer comes over to remind Negan his membership expired and he's not welcome here. Outside, Negan shows Maggie he's wearing an ankle bracelet after he assaulted a guy named Alan. (The men at the other table were friends of Alan's.) Maggie takes him to the batting cages to work off some of that anger — he's good with a bat! — and Negan tells her how he used to be a gym teacher and softball coach, and Alan started seeing one of the girls on his softball team and beating her up. When Negan learned that the girl died by suicide, he broke Alan's jaw — and went to prison for two years as a result. Maggie says she's never hit anyone, but Negan thinks she will... "when something means a lot to you."

What's in the cards for Maggie and Negan?

AMC

As Maggie and Negan walk the streets of New York, he tells her she'd be a great mom, and he knows "because I'm a s**t dad." He has a son, but he never sees him, thinking "the kid's better off without me." Maggie starts to leave for the airport, but Negan tries to convince her to stay — and admits he intended to kill Alan today, showing her a gun. He gives her the gun to hold "for safety" — why isn't she running for her life at this point? — and she decides, "I've tried being good for so long. I think I want to try being happy." And in that spirit, she decides to blow off the flight to see Beth sing. Negan takes her to a Christmas market where she finds a Statue of Liberty snow globe... and also a tarot card reader who promises to foretell her future.

Maggie sits down, and the reader pulls The World card, declaring that Maggie has been to New York in another life. After a few more cards, Negan joins her, and the reader pulls the Wheel of Fortune, telling them they're "in the midst of some major karmic cycle." She examines their hands and finds evidence of "karmic bonds" between them: "You've had several lives together." Negan jokes that this all means they should do some "hanky-panky" — way to spoil the vibe, Negan — and they head to the bar to see Beth sing the Christmas classic "It Came Upon a Midnight Clear," which she and Maggie used to sing as kids. But Negan's face falls when he spots Alan in the crowd.

Negan takes the gun out of Maggie's purse and follows Alan outside, shoving him into an alley and pointing the gun at his head, yelling at him to admit what he did. Maggie runs out to stop Negan, and he relents at first, but then Alan calls her a "little b***h" — and before Negan can shoot him, Maggie punches his lights out. After he runs off, Maggie and Negan share a laugh ("We had something to learn from one another"), and she heads back into the bar while he walks off to call his son.

Maggie and Beth walk home singing together, and Maggie tells her she's ready to sell the farm. They go home to Beth's apartment — and Luis lives in her building, too! But then Maggie gets a call from a loan officer approving her business plan, and she changes her mind: "Maybe what I want can wait a little longer. I mean, it's not like the world is ending tomorrow." (Oof, about that...) Meanwhile, Negan spots Alan on the street and cocks his gun... and we hear a gunshot.

Back in the zombie reality, Maggie's son Hershel runs in to tell her that Negan killed Fabian and sliced Dillard's face in half. Oh man... can't we just keep living in that alternate reality, please?

What'd you think of this very special "Walking Dead: Dead City" episode? Hit the comments to give us your take!
